# Set-up

This markdown prepares the BrainCortex nuclei dataset for analysis. The dataset was downloaded from [docker container](https://hub.docker.com/r/regevlab/demuxem) provided by the original authors. 

The files downloaded are 

- experiment4_human_st_1500_demux_10x.h5 (raw counts, RNA)

- experiment4_human_st_1500_ADT.csv (raw counts, ADT, hashing)

- experiment4_human_st_1500_demux.h5ad (filtered counts)


We will export a `cellranger` like output structure.

## Load data

```{r, warning=FALSE}
# load raw counts (RNA)
counts_raw <- Read10X_h5(here("data/BrainCortex_nuclei_10x/experiment4_human_st_1500_demux_10x.h5"))

#load count filtered h5ad (provided by authors via running the docker container)
#read in using zellconverter to read in python format
sce <- readH5AD(here("data/BrainCortex_nuclei_10x/experiment4_human_st_1500_demux.h5ad"))

#load raw ADT data
tag_mtx <-read_csv(here("data/BrainCortex_nuclei_10x/experiment4_human_st_1500_ADT.csv"), show_col_types = F) %>% column_to_rownames("Antibody")

```

Get filtered barcode from the sce object. 

```{r}
barcodes <- colnames(sce)
```

```{r, include=FALSE}
rm(sce);gc()
```



# Run deMULTIplex2

I am following their vignette on their [GitHub](https://github.com/Gartner-Lab/deMULTIplex2)

*User must provide a tag count matrix where rows are individual cells and columns represent unique sample tags.*


```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
#GET DATA IN ORDER
tag_mtx <- tag_mtx[, barcodes]  #subset to only cells
tag_mtx <- tag_mtx %>% t() #needs to be transposed to match the required format

# RUN FUNCTION
res_demultiplex2 <- demultiplexTags(tag_mtx, # Required, the tag count matrix from your experiment, can be either dense or sparse
                       plot.path = here("output/data/BrainCortex_nuclei_10x/deMULTIplex2_demultiplexing"), # Where to output a summary plot
                       plot.name = "BrainCortex_nuclei_10x", # text append to the name of the summary plot file
                       plot.diagnostics = TRUE) # Whether to output diagnostics plots for each tag
                       # set plot.umap = "none" to not produce any plots
```

```{r}
table(res_demultiplex2$final_assign)
```

Rewrite results to fit in with other structure.

```{r}
meta_sce <- as.data.frame(res_demultiplex2$final_assign) %>%
  dplyr::rename(assignment=`res_demultiplex2$final_assign`) %>% 
  mutate(., doublet_class = case_when(assignment == "multiplet" ~ "doublet", 
                                  assignment == "negative" ~  "remove", 
                                  TRUE ~ "singlet"),
            Barcode_old = rownames(.),
            Barcode = paste0(Barcode_old, "-1"))
```


```{r}
meta_sce$doublet_class %>% table()
```

What does that make the doublet rate (not considering remove section)

```{r}

table(meta_sce$doublet_class)["doublet"]/sum(table(meta_sce$doublet_class)["doublet"] + table(meta_sce$doublet_class)["singlet"])

```

About 10% doublet rate (not including unassigned)


# Prepare `cellranger` output

Make `cellranger` output files for barcodes that were detected as non-empty by the original authors (based on their h5ad object).

## Make SCE object and add QC metrics

```{r}
#change rownames from metadata as they follow the different nomenclature
#making sure this has rowname ensures that creating SCE object would error out if they're not in the same order
rownames(meta_sce) <- meta_sce$Barcode

# all(rownames(meta_sce) == colnames(counts_raw[, meta_sce$Barcode]))

export_sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = c("counts" = counts_raw[, meta_sce$Barcode]), 
                                   colData =meta_sce %>% DataFrame())
  
#add QC metrics
is.mito <- grepl(pattern = "^MT", rownames(export_sce))
is.ribo <- grepl(pattern = "^RP[SL]", rownames(export_sce))
export_sce <- addPerCellQCMetrics(export_sce, subsets = list(mito = is.mito, ribo=is.ribo))

#clean up
new_meta <- export_sce@colData %>% as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename(.,nfeatures_raw = detected, ncount_raw = sum, subsets_mito_percent_raw = subsets_mito_percent, subsets_ribo_percent_raw=subsets_ribo_percent) %>%
  select(., -c("subsets_mito_sum", "subsets_mito_detected", "total", "subsets_ribo_sum", "subsets_ribo_detected"))

export_sce@colData <- new_meta %>% DataFrame()
```

## Export 

Export in `cellranger` output format, including metadata.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#export counts
output_dir <- here("output/data/BrainCortex_nuclei_10x/BrainCortex_nuclei_10x_cellranger/")
DropletUtils::write10xCounts(path = output_dir,
                             x = counts(export_sce),
                             version = "3",
                             overwrite = T)
#and export metadata
write_tsv(x= as.data.frame(export_sce@colData), file = paste0(output_dir, "metadata.tsv"),
          col_names = T)

```


# Prepare *empty droplets* `cellranger` output

Having an object that represent just the empty droplets is very useful when performing ambient RNA correction, so we'll export an empty droplets object in `cellranger` format as well. 


We'll use all the barcodes that were not considered non-empty (so empty) by the original authors. 

```{r, eval=FALSE}
#subset counts
empty_object <- counts_raw[, !(colnames(counts_raw) %in% export_sce$Barcode)]
```



```{r, eval=FALSE}
#export counts
output_dir <- here("output/data/BrainCortex_nuclei_10x/BrainCortex_nuclei_10x_emptyObject")
DropletUtils::write10xCounts(path = output_dir,
                             x = empty_object,
                             version = "3",
                             overwrite = T)
```
